name: Battle of Tsushima

phases.title: The fleets sight each other
phases.text: The Russians steamed north-north-east in columns, the main group on the right, the left column and the Nikolai I group to the west and the auxiliaries behind. The Japanese main group came down from the north-east heading south-south-west.

phases.title: The Japanese turn in sequence and open fire
phases.text: Mikasa turned about and the ships behind her followed in sequence to head north-north-east. The Russian main group had shifted left to cover the left column, and the Russians opened fire on the Japanese as they turned.

phases.title: The Japanese cross ahead of the Russian column
phases.text: Mikasa and her line turned north-east and then east to cross the T, and the Russian left column turned north-east and then east-south-east in response. Oslyabya was set on fire, and Knyaz Suvorov caught fire and fell away from the line.

phases.title: Aleksandr III turns the Russian main group north
phases.text: With the Japanese 1st division completely overtaking the Russian battleships heading east-south-east, Aleksandr III turned to the north, with Borodino and Oryol following.

phases.title: The Japanese 1st division reverses; the 2nd attacks
phases.text: The 1st division made an immediate left U-turn on the spot to head west-north-west, in reverse order. The 2nd division continued south-east and then south-west, attacking the secondary Russian warships.

phases.title: Aleksandr III turns south-east
phases.text: Aleksandr III, apparently giving up fleeing north, turned south-east, with Borodino and Oryol following. The Russian main group thus reversed its northward course and stood on the opposite heading to the Japanese line.

phases.title: The 1st division loses sight of the main group
phases.text: Nisshin and the five ships made another immediate left U-turn, and the 1st division headed north-east in normal order, with Mikasa first and Nisshin last. The 1st division lost sight of the Russian main group in the smoke and mist.

phases.title: The 2nd division finds the main group
phases.text: The Japanese 2nd division found the Russian main group close to where the 3rd Squadron, the 5th and 6th divisions, was attacking the Russian auxiliaries protected by cruisers.

phases.title: The Japanese main group catches the Russian main group
phases.text: After losing sight of the Russian main group in smoke and mist, the 1st division caught up with it heading north-west and fired on the leading Aleksandr III. The 5th division, part of the 3rd Squadron, had been attacking the Russian auxiliaries.

phases.title: Torpedo attacks in the night
phases.text: The 1st division left the battleground and the 2nd and 4th were ordered to gather in the north, leaving the destroyers and torpedo boats to attack in the dark. The attacks forced the Russians to turn west, and they were dispersed in small groups.

phases.title: The Russian remnant is sighted and surrounded
phases.text: The remaining Russian ships were sighted heading north-east. Tōgō's battleships moved to surround Nebogatov's remaining squadron south of the island of Takeshima, the 1st division approaching from the north.

phases.title: Nebogatov surrenders
phases.text: The Japanese battleships opened main battery fire at 12,000 metres. Nebogatov signalled surrender at 10:34, and Tōgō accepted it at 10:45 once the Russian ships had stopped.

note: The plan shows the whole two-day action as a sketch. The accounts give courses and the order of ships, not distances, so every position is approximate. The Japanese destroyer and torpedo boat attack, said to come from the north, east and west, is drawn as one block in the north. The accounts do not say where the Japanese battleships went when they left the battleground in the evening, so they are drawn withdrawing northwards. The Russian main group included Oryol, which was later among the ships that surrendered; the plan does not follow her out of the main group.
